prompt:
Use case: realistic Hanzi learning photographic source triptych for later cropping.
Scene/backdrop: three separate landscape photographs of real seashells on quiet natural beach sand, stacked vertically edge to edge in one 1024 x 1792 image. Exactly three equal-height horizontal rows; straight full-width scene changes at one-third and two-thirds of the image height (approximately y=597 and y=1195). Each row is its own independent photograph, not one continuous scene.
Subjects in exact top-to-bottom order: TOP: one real scallop shell with an unmistakable broad fan shape, radiating ribs, natural irregular cream and muted rose coloration, the complete shell visible. MIDDLE: one real spiral conch shell, photographed at a three-quarter angle so its spiraling pointed spire and natural opening are clearly identifiable, complete shell visible. BOTTOM: one real clam shell with exactly two matching valves still joined at their natural hinge and resting partly open; both valves and their physical hinge connection clearly visible, the complete joined shell visible.
Style/medium: highly photorealistic close-up camera photographs of actual physical objects, with mineral grain, chalky weathering, tiny chips, fine growth lines and naturally uneven shell surfaces. Natural shell material, correct anatomy, credible real-world proportions and scale. Sharp subject detail and gently quieter backgrounds, never glossy synthetic perfection.
Composition/framing: each shell is the clear main subject, centered within its own wide landscape row, entirely inside that row with comfortable margin on all sides. Keep every shell well away from row boundaries; no subject crosses a scene change. The scenes fill all pixels to the outside edges.
Lighting: soft natural daylight, realistic contact shadows on the sand, coherent physical shading and depth.
Constraints: no people, extra shells, decorative props, text, letters, labels, logos, watermarks, borders, dividing lines or gutters. No cartoon, illustration, painting, CGI, 3D render, stylized geometry, plastic-looking shells or plastic-looking sand. Exactly three rows, equal height.
reviewNotes: Read and visually inspected full source: three edge-to-edge rows with clean scene boundaries approximately at y=597 and y=1195. Correct subject order: fan-shaped scallop, spiral conch with visible opening, two joined clam valves. Complete subjects have margins; convincing natural shell grain, weathering, sand texture and contact shadows. No text, gutters, borders or logos. Integer row heights necessarily differ by one pixel at 1792px total height. No cropping performed.
